doc.title: Howie Shear interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2014

chapter: Joan Rivers Show and Woody Herman
title: The big trumpet players and juggling jobs on the road
summary: Shear names the top L.A. trumpeters and describes hiding absences while juggling the Joan Rivers Show and Reno and Tahoe gigs.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Chuck Findley, Jerry Hey, Gary Grant. They did a lot of the Michael Jackson stuff and the Quincy Jones stuff with Michael Jackson. That was a big section. And Malcolm McNab is the movie guy in L.A. There’s a lot of players that had been in the scene way before I got there. And if for some reason they couldn’t make something because something came up, they would still get called again. But if I as a young guy that walked into town and got called for something and I couldn’t make it, and I called up the contractor and told him that, he might be a little bothered and he would either say well I’ll get somebody, and you may not hear from them again. It’s a tough call, to overbook yourself.
I’ve had guys tell me that they had to be wary about going on the road, even if it was a good deal, because by the time they got back —

Out of sight, out of mind. So I would never tell people I was out for a week or a month or six months. When I was out of town for long periods of time, which I don’t do anymore, there were no cell phones. So now you don’t ever have to tell anybody you left town, you just get the call, and you could be in Ames, Iowa and say yeah, I’m around the corner, but I can’t meet you now because I have a — you know you fly home. When I was doing the Joan Rivers Show, I was the musical arranger for the Joan Rivers late night show, and I would get called to do, oh two, three, four week things in Lake Tahoe or Reno, for the show I was affiliated with, and I wouldn’t tell the Joan Rivers Show. I flew up — I did the show in Tahoe or Reno and I’d sometimes, every day during the day. Fly in, hand in music, and then get a sub for my Reno or Tahoe show for three or four days, because I played in the band too. And I was doing double duty. And I didn’t have a phone really.
But I would make sure that neither would know I was out of town. So you’re doing a lot of juggling.
You didn’t learn that at Fredonia. Or maybe you did.

Which party to go to. So you learn how to do that. As long as you’re covering yourself, and the show in Reno and Tahoe was not a big deal and there’s plenty of musicians in those towns that needed the work. But I would never turn down the Joan Rivers Show to stay in Reno but I would always get a sub for Reno for three or four days and come back to L.A. And I was flying back and forth for a long time. It was kind of fun because I was in my early 30s and I had a lot of energy. And it was kind of nice living that lifestyle never knowing where I’d be on a given day or night.
